target_customer: Frontier AI labs, robotics companies, surgeons and industrial teams that need human interaction data to train physical AI
problem: Robots learn mostly from video, which lacks the force, touch and muscle effort behind human movement. Preload sells synchronized multisensory recordings of people doing tasks to fill that gap.
business_model: Data collection and dataset sales for robotics training, with evaluation and deployment tools (per the company site); pricing not stated
product_category: Physical AI training data hardware (egocentric camera, tactile glove, EMG band)

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom hardware stack that fuses egocentric video, tactile glove and EMG streams in sync, plus ingestion pipelines. The founders have neural signal and BCI hardware experience, which lowers risk, but hardware iteration with three people is hard.

defensibility.rationale: Multimodal EMG plus tactile data is rarer than video, but well funded rivals already collect egocentric data and glove hardware is sold off the shelf. A data moat only appears if datasets compound.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to say; as of November 2026 no incumbent action against Preload is reported.

market_need_then: Robotics labs in 2026 are buying large egocentric human datasets, shown by multiple seed rounds in the category (Human Archive $8.2M, Maxinsights $30M). Touch and force data are named as the missing modality by vendors in the space.

brand_strength.rationale: Newly launched with no press about the brand found; 'preload' is a common technical term so search distinctiveness is limited.

outcome_analysis: Preload is a Fall 2026 YC company that has just started, so no outcome exists yet. The founders' neural signal and BCI background fits the EMG and tactile angle, while funded competitors already sell egocentric data, so differentiation on touch and force data will decide whether it raises beyond the YC deal.
